title: Dependencies and Lifecycle Rules

header.html: 4f Define resource dependencies in configuration, including depends_on and the create_before_destroy lifecycle rule
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1The dependency graph

Terraform builds a dependency graph of all the resources, data sources and modules, then walks the graph.

Fact Detail
Independent resources Created in parallel (by default up to 10 at a time, set with -parallelism)
Dependent resources Created after what they depend on
Destroy In reverse order: dependents first
terraform graph Prints the graph in DOT format

2Implicit and explicit dependencies

Kind How Example
Implicit A reference to another object subnet_id = aws_subnet.main.id
Explicit The depends_on meta-argument depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.app] 
resource "aws_instance" "app" {
  ami           = "ami-0abcdef1234567890"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"

  depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.app]
}

Use depends_on only when there is a hidden dependency that no reference shows (for example a permission the application needs at start-up). It takes a list of resource or module addresses.

Exam tip

. References are preferred; depends_on is the exception. Over-using depends_on makes plans less precise because Terraform then assumes everything may have changed.

3The lifecycle block

The lifecycle meta-argument changes how Terraform creates, updates and destroys one resource.

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-0abcdef1234567890"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
    prevent_destroy       = false
    ignore_changes        = [tags]
  }
}
Rule Effect
create_before_destroy When a resource must be replaced, create the new one first, then destroy the old one (default is destroy first); avoids downtime and suits resources whose names must be unique
prevent_destroy Any plan that would destroy the resource fails with an error; protects critical data
ignore_changes Ignore changes to the listed arguments, for example tags changed by another tool; all ignores every argument
replace_triggered_by Replace this resource when another resource or attribute changes
precondition, postcondition Custom checks (Module 9)
Replacement order Plan symbol
Default: destroy, then create -/+
create_before_destroy: create, then destroy +/-

prevent_destroy does not stop terraform destroy from being planned; it makes the plan fail. Removing the resource block from the configuration also removes the protection.

Exam tip

. create_before_destroy = new first, old later. prevent_destroy = error instead of destroy. ignore_changes = accept outside changes to chosen arguments.

4Forcing replacement

terraform apply -replace="aws_instance.web" replaces that resource in one run. It replaces the old terraform taint command, which is deprecated.

Exam tip

. Explicit depends_on is a last resort. A reference already creates the order; add depends_on only for a hidden dependency.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1One resource uses an attribute of another resource. How does Terraform know the order?

  • ABy the implicit dependency from the reference
  • BBy the order of the blocks in the file
  • CBy the alphabetical order of the names
  • DBy a depends_on block that is always required
Show the answer

Answer: A. A reference creates an implicit dependency, and Terraform orders the work from the graph.

S2An application needs an IAM policy to exist before it starts, but the resource does not reference the policy. What should be added?

  • AA provider alias
  • BA count meta-argument on the resource
  • CA depends_on meta-argument
  • DA data block
Show the answer

Answer: C. depends_on declares an explicit dependency when no reference shows it.

S3A resource must be replaced without downtime, and the new object should exist before the old one is removed. Which lifecycle rule fits?

  • Aprevent_destroy
  • Bignore_changes
  • Creplace_triggered_by on the resource
  • Dcreate_before_destroy
Show the answer

Answer: D. create_before_destroy creates the replacement first, then destroys the old object.

S4A team wants Terraform to refuse any plan that would delete a production database. Which rule fits?

  • Aignore_changes set to all
  • Bprevent_destroy set to true
  • Ccreate_before_destroy set to true
  • Ddepends_on set to the database
Show the answer

Answer: B. prevent_destroy makes any plan that would destroy the resource fail with an error.

S5Another tool changes the tags on instances, and Terraform should stop reporting this as a change. Which rule fits?

  • Aignore_changes with the tags argument
  • Breplace_triggered_by with the tags argument
  • Cprevent_destroy for the instances
  • Dcreate_before_destroy for the tags
Show the answer

Answer: A. ignore_changes lists arguments whose outside changes Terraform will ignore.

S6Which option forces one resource to be replaced in a single apply?

  • Aterraform taint followed by apply
  • Bterraform refresh with the address
  • Cterraform fmt with the address
  • Dterraform apply -replace with the resource address
Show the answer

Answer: D. The -replace option replaces the named resource; taint is deprecated.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How does Terraform order resources?

Show the answer

By a dependency graph built from references and depends_on.

R2When is depends_on needed?

Show the answer

For a hidden dependency that no reference shows.

R3What does create_before_destroy do?

Show the answer

Creates the new object before destroying the old one.

R4What does prevent_destroy do?

Show the answer

Makes any plan that would destroy the resource fail.

R5What does ignore_changes do?

Show the answer

Ignores outside changes to the listed arguments.

R6What replaced terraform taint?

Show the answer

apply with the -replace option.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Graph implicit (references) and explicit (depends_on); parallel when independent; destroy in reverse
lifecycle create_before_destroy, prevent_destroy, ignore_changes, replace_triggered_by, conditions
Replace -/+ default (destroy first), +/- with create_before_destroy; apply -replace
